High level answers up front:
- Region residency: For private VPC deployments we pin all object and block storage to the customer-selected region. Snapshots are stored in the same region by default; cross-region replication is opt-in and requires a signed request and a specific config flag.
- BYOK/KMS: We support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; the key material remains in the customer KMS (supported cloud providers) and Redwood holds only the key reference/ARN. We can also integrate with HSM-backed KMS via standard APIs.
- Deletion & proof: We have a three-stage sanitization flow (logical revoke, data sanitize, metadata purge) and we can produce a proof package containing job IDs, timestamped audit records, and hashed manifests for key objects.

I've attached a one-page checklist and a KMS key-flow diagram to give your auditors something concrete. Neha — can you add the deletion SLAs and the exact items we can commit to in writing? Karthik — please confirm there are no hidden offsite backup copies for the pilot.

Tom / Laura — quick technical write-up from Security on what we can provide for the pilot and the standard Private/VPC behavior. I've kept it focused so your auditors can consume it directly.

1) Residency and backups
- Primary storage (object + block) is provisioned in the customer-selected region and bound to the customer's VPC endpoint. No snapshots or automated backups are shipped outside that region by default.
- Cross-region replication is disabled unless enabled explicitly in the account config and only after a documented request signed by the customer.

2) Keys and encryption
- BYOK: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Redwood stores only the key reference (ARN/URI); cryptographic operations are proxied to the customer KMS.
- Key material never transits Redwood-managed control plane. If you use a customer HSM, we will configure the invocation path so that encryption/decryption occurs within the customer's KMS/HSM boundary.

3) Deletion / sanitization flow (private deployment specifics)
- Stage A — Logical revoke (T0): Access tokens and service-level pointers to the tenant are revoked immediately; live API responses will no longer surface tenant data. Target: within 24 hours.
- Stage B — Data sanitization (T1): Background jobs target objects, DB rows, and KV stores to securely delete or overwrite primary copies. For object stores we perform object-level deletes followed by a metadata manifest update. Target: 7 days for standard tenant sizes in pilot (typical pilot < 5 TB).
- Stage C — Metadata purge & manifest (T2): Index entries, logs referencing PII, and retained metadata are purged and a final manifest of removed items is assembled. Target: 30 days for full manifest completion.

4) Proof artifacts we can produce
- Deletion job IDs + timestamps (job-run-UUIDs).
- SHA256 manifest of top-level objects prior to deletion and a post-deletion manifest (where possible) to demonstrate object IDs no longer resolve.
- Audit log exports showing KMS decrypt calls, admin actions, and deletion job execution.
- Snapshot listing confirming no active snapshots remain (if snapshots existed).
- Optional: third-party attestation engagement deliverable (we coordinate procurement).

5) Offsite/backups & retention exceptions
- For Private/VPC we do not keep vendor-controlled offsite backups for tenant data unless explicitly contracted (rare for pilots). Any backup or snapshot that exists (e.g., scheduled infra-managed snapshot) is documented and included in the proof package.

6) Evidence delivery
- We can produce a compressed proof package (CSV of deleted object prefixes, job-ids log, audit log excerpt) and deliver via a signed link or secure Share (DocuSign or secure S3 pre-signed link). Template: redwood-deletion-proof-template.csv

Notes/constraints
- The stated timelines assume standard pilot scale and no legal hold. Legal holds require escalation and will pause Stage B/C until lifted.
- For extremely large tenants (>50 TB) we provide a scoped timeline during onboarding.

If you want, Marcus can run a short smoke test on a staging tenant and produce a sample proof package so you can validate the artifacts format before the pilot.

-Neha

Tom — short answers and a proposed contract-friendly SLA you can drop into the DPA. Neha has reviewed and approved this language.

1) Attestation: We can provide a signed attestation for SH-PILOT-01 confirming the delivered proof package corresponds to removal actions executed by Redwood. Attestation will include job IDs, timestamps, and a statement of the scope of deletion. Standard attestation add-on: we bill a one-time attestation fee or can include it under an enterprise addendum.

2) Contract SLA (recommended DPA language) — sample: 
"Upon Customer-initiated tenant termination, Redwood will: (a) complete Stage A (logical revoke) within 24 hours; (b) complete Stage B (data sanitization) within 7 calendar days for tenants <= 5 TB, or provide a scoped timeline for larger tenants; and (c) provide a final proof package and completion manifest within 30 calendar days. Redwood will provide the proof package via a secure, signed transfer and make reasonable efforts to provide a signed attestation within 10 business days of proof package delivery if requested."

3) KMS logs: Yes — KMS audit exports will include the customer key ARN and timestamps for decrypt/encrypt API calls as supplied by the cloud provider's audit logs (we include them verbatim in the proof package). We do not retain key material.

- Laura to share the attestation template and the final checklist for your legal team to review.
